title: Pilot: This Meeting Could Be an Email
logline: A 1987 ghost clerk sits through a modern meeting and delivers the verdict: it could have been an email.
hook: Statement hook: absurd claim to camera in first second

scenes.keyframe_prompt: Vertical 9:16 shot inside a modern open-space office, a glass meeting room at night with a laptop video call on a large screen showing blurred tiny faces. The same man from the reference image (ghost Walt) sits at the end of the conference table, semi-transparent with a cool cyan-blue glow, mustard-brown 1987 suit and paperclip tie, hands folded, looking straight into the camera with a deadpan weary expression, medium close-up chest up. Cold fluorescent light, warm desk lamp accent, photorealistic.
scenes.motion_prompt: Static camera with a slow push-in over 6 seconds. Walt slowly blinks, leans slightly toward the camera and says in a dry low voice: "I've been dead for thirty-nine years, and this meeting could still have been an email." Faint office hum, quiet laptop notification ping.
scenes.dialogue: I've been dead for thirty-nine years, and this meeting could still have been an email.

scenes.keyframe_prompt: Vertical 9:16, same glass meeting room, tight close-up of the same man from the reference image (ghost Walt), cyan glow, glasses with blue tape, moustache. He holds a single paperclip between two fingers, tired smirk, the blurred video call glowing behind him, shallow depth of field, cold fluorescent light.
scenes.motion_prompt: Close-up, camera still. Walt sighs, the ceiling lamp above him flickers once, he places the paperclip neatly on the table and says flatly to the camera: "Noted. I'm still clocked in." Soft table click, office hum.
